bipl5

An R Package for Reactive Biplots



Ruan Buys
Sugnet Lubbe
Luca Steyn

2026-05-19

Today’s Goal

bipl5 turns PCA, CVA, regression and PCO biplots into interactive Plotly htmlwidgets.

In this webinar we cover three things:

  • Build a biplot directly with the standalone bipl5 workflow.
  • Wrap an existing biplotEZ object and render it with bipl5.
  • Drop the resulting widget straight into a Quarto presentation.

All examples use the iris data set.

Function Map

Construct

  • init_biplot()
  • scale_mds()
  • format_samples()
  • colorpal()
  • Symbol_List()

Wrap biplotEZ

Use this when a biplot is already built with biplotEZ::PCA(), CVA(), regress() or PCO().

  • wrap_bipl5()

Traverse

  • plot()
  • append_mdsDisplay()
  • remove_mdsDisplay()
  • extract()
  • overlay_fit()

Standalone Construction

Part 1 — building a biplot from raw data

Build the Biplot

init_biplot() ingests the data and scale_mds() chooses the method and subspace. Grouping aesthetics are set in the pipeline with format_samples().

library(bipl5)
library(biplotEZ)

bp_standalone <- init_biplot(iris) |>
  scale_mds(type = "pca", eigenvectors = c(1, 2)) |>
  format_samples(stratify = "col", by = Species, col = species_cols)

bp_standalone
#> bipl5_biplot [PCA] 
#> <U+251C><U+2500><U+2500> mdsDisplay_12 [PC 1 & 2] <bipl5_mdsDisplay>
#> <U+2502>   <U+251C><U+2500><U+2500> Data <bipl5_data>
#> <U+2502>   <U+2502>   <U+251C><U+2500><U+2500> sample_coordinates  [150 x 2]
#> <U+2502>   <U+2502>   <U+251C><U+2500><U+2500> axes_coordinates  [4 axes]
#> <U+2502>   <U+2502>   <U+2514><U+2500><U+2500> translated_axes_coordinates
#> <U+2502>   <U+251C><U+2500><U+2500> trace_data  [31 traces]
#> <U+2502>   <U+2514><U+2500><U+2500> annotations  [80 items]
#> <U+2514><U+2500><U+2500> fit_measures <bipl5_fitmeasures>
#>     <U+251C><U+2500><U+2500> CumPred  [5 traces]
#>     <U+251C><U+2500><U+2500> CumAd  [4 traces]
#>     <U+251C><U+2500><U+2500> VarExp  [5 traces]
#>     <U+251C><U+2500><U+2500> Scree  [1 traces]
#>     <U+2514><U+2500><U+2500> fit_table_12  [PC 1 & 2]

The Standalone Plot

stage(bp_standalone, height = 560)

Styling the Sample Layer

format_samples() restyles the rendered sample layer — no rebuild needed.

bp_species <- bp_standalone |>
  format_samples(
    stratify = "col",
    by = Species,
    col = species_cols
  ) |>
  format_samples(
    stratify = "symbol",
    by = Species,
    pch = species_pch
  )

Colour and plotting character are set per group from the Species factor.

Styled Biplot

stage(bp_species, height = 560)

A Second Stratifying Variable

format_samples() can stratify by two different variables at once — colour by one, plotting symbol by another. The sample traces are rebuilt internally as the observed Species × Band combinations, with a separate legend section per variable.

iris_banded <- iris
iris_banded$Band <- factor(
  rep(c("A", "B", "C", "D"), length.out = nrow(iris_banded))
)

bp_dual <- init_biplot(iris_banded) |>
  scale_mds(type = "pca", eigenvectors = c(1, 2)) |>
  format_samples(stratify = "col", by = Species, col = species_cols) |>
  format_samples(stratify = "symbol", by = Band, pch = c(15, 16, 17, 18))

Two-Variable Stratification

stage(bp_dual, height = 560)

Adding More Displays

A single object can hold several displays. append_mdsDisplay() adds another eigenvector pair to the dropdown.

bp_multi <- bp_species |>
  append_mdsDisplay(c(1, 3)) |>
  append_mdsDisplay(c(2, 3))

names(bp_multi$meta$pc_info)
#> [1] "mdsDisplay_12" "mdsDisplay_13" "mdsDisplay_23"

Multi-Display Biplot

Switch eigenvector pairs live with the dropdown in the top-left of the widget.

stage(bp_multi, height = 530)

Traversing the Object

extract() and remove_mdsDisplay() navigate a multi-display object.

bp_one_view   <- extract(bp_multi, mdsDisplay_13)
bp_without_23 <- remove_mdsDisplay(bp_multi, mdsDisplay_23)

iris_scores <- extract(bp_multi, mdsDisplay_12$Data$sample_coordinates)
head(iris_scores, 5)
#>        [,1]       [,2]
#> 1 -2.684126 -0.3193972
#> 2 -2.714142  0.1770012
#> 3 -2.888991  0.1449494
#> 4 -2.745343  0.3182990
#> 5 -2.728717 -0.3267545

An Extracted View

bp_one_view keeps only the PC 1 – PC 3 display pulled from the multi-display object.

stage(bp_one_view, height = 530)

Fit-Panel Layout

overlay_fit() stores a plotting preference: render the fit summaries as an overlay across the full plot width rather than in a side panel.

bp_overlay <- bp_multi |>
  overlay_fit()

Open the fit panel from the widget toolbar to see the effect.

Overlay Fit

stage(bp_overlay, height = 560)

biplotEZ Wrapper

Part 2 — when you already have a biplotEZ pipeline

Wrapping a biplotEZ Pipeline

Use wrap_bipl5() when your starting point is an existing biplotEZ pipeline.

bp_ez_pca <- biplotEZ::biplot(iris[, 1:4]) |>
  biplotEZ::PCA() |>
  wrap_bipl5()

wrap_bipl5() consumes the biplotEZ object and returns a bipl5 object — ready for plot() and every traversing function.

Wrapped PCA Biplot

stage(bp_ez_pca, height = 560)

Wrapped CVA — Build

The same wrapper handles a CVA biplot; just pass the class variable.

bp_ez_cva <- biplotEZ::biplot(iris[, 1:4]) |>
  biplotEZ::CVA(classes = iris$Species) |>
  wrap_bipl5()

Wrapped CVA Biplot

stage(bp_ez_cva, height = 560)

Regression Biplot — Build

A regression biplot calibrates axes onto an externally supplied sample map. Here the target is a Sammon scaling of the rock data.

target_map <- MASS::sammon(dist(scale(rock)), trace = FALSE)$points

bp_ez_reg <- biplotEZ::biplot(rock) |>
  biplotEZ::regress(Z = target_map) |>
  wrap_bipl5()

Regression Biplot

stage(bp_ez_reg, height = 560)

Spline Axes — Build

PCO(axes = "splines") calibrates non-linear axes — useful when a straight axis would distort how a variable maps onto the display.

bp_ez_spline <- biplotEZ::biplot(rock, scale = TRUE) |>
  biplotEZ::PCO(axes = "splines") |>
  wrap_bipl5()

Spline-Axis Biplot

stage(bp_ez_spline, height = 560)

Alpha-Bag Biplot — Build

biplotEZ enhancements survive the wrap. Adding alpha.bags() to the pipeline draws an alpha bag around each group, and wrap_bipl5() carries it through.

bp_ez_bags <- biplotEZ::biplot(iris[, 1:4], group.aes = iris$Species) |>
  biplotEZ::PCA() |>
  biplotEZ::alpha.bags() |>
  wrap_bipl5()

Alpha-Bag Biplot

stage(bp_ez_bags, height = 560)
